The macOS CI failure was at test setup: std::os::unix::ffi::OsStrExt created a recovery-\xff leaf, and std::os file creation returned OS error 92 (Illegal byte sequence) on macOS before enumeration ran. Replaced that fixture with the portable dangling recovery-symlink and added an explicit read_optional rejection assertion. This retains the test's safety claims: repeated scans use the held directory after selected-path replacement; matching unreadable managed entries are observed without opening/following them; removal and directory entries are reflected by fresh scans; the substituted outside directory and its bytes are unchanged. It intentionally no longer makes a non-UTF-8 filename claim on macOS.

A CI pass will establish only core tests/cargo build, not actual macOS runtime or native WebKit close behavior. Next bounded task: independent review sj-86z and inspect the macOS CI result.
